# Project Configuration Editing

Use this protocol when the user requests a project configuration change. It does not expand the assigned role's permissions: a read-only role remains read-only.

1. Establish scope from the request and conversation. An explicit lasting preference or a request made while editing configuration authorizes persistence without another save confirmation. A temporary request applies only to the current operation. Clarify an ambiguous scope; never silently make it permanent. An Agent's own recommendation requires user confirmation before persistence.
2. Query effective values with `xirang config project` and read `xirang config` for supported fields and scope. Reuse the existing matching field instead of adding a duplicate preference. If no supported field expresses the request, explain the limitation; do not add an ineffective key. For example, “以后默认展开三层” or “改成三层” while discussing configuration updates `architecture.outline.definitionDepth`; “这次展开三层” uses a one-operation override. This is Definition loading depth, not browser expansion or tree cropping.
3. Locate the active project file (.yaml takes precedence over .yml). Preserve unrelated user values, comments and layout while editing the corresponding field. CLI commands other than setup do not create or repair project configuration; the user may explicitly delegate recovery to an Agent. Ordinary preference edits do not increment `configVersion`, which is managed by setup/update; never change a version number merely to bypass migration.
4. Reload the relevant effective values after editing and validate the result. Use `xirang config check` for configuration/reference diagnostics when applicable; it does not prove natural-language rules were executed. Read the new values even if earlier configuration was cached in the conversation.
5. Briefly report the field, before/after values, affected operation and when it takes effect. Do not require a full check report for every edit. External file edits do not automatically refresh an Agent session.
